① 'subjectively' — modifies the noun 'probability', which requires an adjective. 'subjectively probability weight' is wrong — should be 'subjective probability weight'. ②likely(adjective complement, correct), ③the more(parallel comparative, correct), ④optimistic(adjective, correct).

② 'isn't' — 'Events that...isn't likely' is wrong. 'Events' (plural) requires 'aren't': 'Events that...aren't likely'. ①to know(infinitive, correct), ③tend to(correct), ④the largest(superlative, correct).

② 'fade' — 'Low-probability events tend to fade more into decisions than they should' doesn't make sense. 'Fade' = disappear; passage says 'factor more into decisions' = play a larger role. 'Fade' is contextually wrong. ①subjective(correct), ③We overestimate(correct), ④optimistic(correct).

Blank: 'Low-probability events tend to __'. Passage: 'factor more into decisions than they should' = ④의사 결정에 실제보다 더 크게 반영된다. ①정확한 확률 계산에 기여 (wrong), ②사람들의 관심을 끌지 못 (wrong — they do get attention), ③의사 결정에 영향 미치지 않음 (opposite of passage).

내용 일치: ①사람들은 저확률 사건의 가능성을 과대평가하는 경향이 있다 — TRUE (passage: 'We overestimate the likelihood of these low-probability events'). ②항상 일치: FALSE. ③25% 이상이 저확률: FALSE (UP TO 25%). ④175분의 1: FALSE (175 million).

내용 일치: ②미국의 대형 복권 당첨 확률은 1억 7천5백만분의 1 수준이다 — TRUE (passage: 'on the order of one in 175 million'). ①주관적 가중치 측정 불가: NOT stated. ③저확률 사건 적게 반영: FALSE (more than they should). ④객관 1%=주관 1%: FALSE (the whole point is they diverge).

주제: ④저확률 사건에 대한 인간의 과대평가 경향 — The passage is entirely about how humans overestimate low-probability events. ①복권 산업 경제 효과: lottery is just an example. ②확률 이론 수학적 기초: not the topic. ③감정의 역할: not discussed.

요지 (English): ①'People systematically overweight unlikely events in decision-making' — This captures 'low-probability events factor more into decisions than they should' = overweighting. ②'Lottery systems exploit statistical ignorance': not the argument (no mention of exploitation). ③'Subjective probability always converges with objective': WRONG (the whole point is divergence). ④'Low-probability events deserve more attention': WRONG (they ALREADY get too much attention).

'on the order of one in 175 million' — this describes an astronomically small probability. The passage uses this to illustrate that despite such low odds, lottery players are optimistic. ②'An astronomically small probability people still overvalue' captures both the scale AND the main theme. ①'reasonable chance': wrong (175M is not reasonable). ③'statistical error': wrong. ④'exact mathematical odds published': too literal, misses the point.

'Low-probability events tend to factor more into decisions than they should.' — 'they' refers to 'low-probability events' (the subject of the sentence). ③저확률 사건들. ①의사 결정들 (wrong — decisions is the object), ②객관적 확률들 (wrong), ④주관적 가중치들 (wrong).

'In general, the smaller the probability, the more we overestimate its likelihood.' — 'its' refers back to the antecedent. The nearest singular noun it could refer to is 'the probability' (from 'the smaller the probability'). ④확률의. ①저확률 사건의 (plural events, not singular), ②과대평가의 (can't overestimate overestimation), ③의사 결정의 (wrong context).
